lines.text: It's two forty in the morning. Alarms just went off on five services, across two teams.
Only one of them is the real problem. Which one?
In a modern company, one broken service sets off alarms everywhere it is connected.
The usual rule, trust the loudest or the first alarm, picks the right service only forty percent of the time. And every minute of guessing is a minute customers can't pay.
This is RootCause. An AI on-call engineer that finds the one real cause, explains it in plain words, and fixes it once you say yes.
Under the hood, everything is a graph in FalkorDB. Every request becomes nodes and edges: the services, the calls between them, the teams that own them, the customers who use them, and every change.
When alarms fire, blame flows along the calls. A failing service blames the one it depends on.
Alarms that are connected become one incident. That's connected components.
PageRank finds where all the blame ends up. The shortest path through the blame is the evidence, and a change made minutes earlier is the why.
Here's a real run, replayed from the OpenTelemetry Demo shop. Customers on the left, every service grouped by the team that owns it. The moving dots are real requests.
A fault hits. Alarms on five services, across two teams. RootCause messages the on-call engineer, like a colleague on WhatsApp.
It knows the alarms are one problem, and its agent walks the graph, step by step.

Root cause: the product catalog. Its own requests fail first, the blame flows to it, and a feature flag changed just before. The database looks slow too, but nothing changed there, so RootCause calls it a symptom.
It also shows who is hurt: customers browsing and viewing products.
Should I fix this? It proposes the lowest risk fix, switching that flag back, and says exactly what it touches.
One yes, and it applies the fix and watches every alarm clear.
Recovered, verified, and the incident report is written. Errors are back to zero.

We tested it blind. Fifteen random faults on the real demo. RootCause named the right service first eighty seven percent of the time, in a median of fifty three seconds. The usual alarm rules managed forty percent.

Why a graph? Because what broke is a question about connections. Connected components turn alarms into one incident. PageRank finds the cause. Breadth first search shows what a fix will touch. And shared signal patterns help it remember.
RootCause. Graph algorithms find the cause, an agent explains it, and a human says yes.
